# Barrel generation

Read when a package's generated `src/index.ts` barrel, its `exportsGeneration` option, or the generator behind them is in question. `SKILL.md` says only that the build generates barrels; this page is how, and why generation is unguarded.

## Barrels are generated by the build, not in front of it

tsdown bundles from `src/index.ts` and never writes it — its default entry only checks the file exists. A library normally commits a hand-written barrel as its chosen public API; here every module with an export is public (the `file-organization` skill, "One export per file"), so the file is generated and gitignored instead, and the generator is ours.

`getTsdownConfiguration` runs `generateExports` from a `build:prepare` hook, so no manifest repeats the command. What a package generates is the `exportsGeneration` option — `"typescript"` by default, `"vue"` for the package that ships components, `"none"` for one that names its own entrypoints and would otherwise get a barrel nothing is an entry for. There is no separate command: a package's build is the regeneration, and cheap enough to be the only one.

The barrel is one `export * from` line per module under `src`, sorted, leaving out the tests (`NON_SOURCE_SUFFIXES`), ambient `.d.ts` files, and any module with no export — a CLI or a test setup is a program, and listing it would run it on every import of the package. Whether a module exports is read from rolldown's own oxc parse (`parseSync`'s `staticExports`, which counts a type-only export), so no TypeScript program is loaded and a package's barrel costs milliseconds. The `"vue"` answer first writes `src/components/index.ts`, one `export { default as <Name> }` per `.vue` file, which the source barrel then lists like any other module.

What makes it work looks redundant until it is gone:

- **`entry` is stated even though it is tsdown's own default.** Left unset, tsdown checks that `src/index.ts` exists _while resolving the config_, before any hook runs — so a package whose barrel is not on disk dies with `No input files`, which is every fresh clone. A literal entry reaches rolldown, which reads it after `build:prepare`.
- **The option is a union of literals, never an enum.** `packages/configuration` reaches its own source through `#src/*`, and tsdown loads a config with Node's strip-only type stripping: an enum fails outright with `TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode`. A type erases to nothing.

## A name exported twice is a type error, never a silent drop

Every line is `export *`, so two modules exporting the same name are an ambiguity TypeScript reports as `TS2308` — in the package's own typecheck, and in every consumer resolving its source. That is the reason the barrel is not ctix's any more: ctix resolved the same collision by dropping the name from the barrel with a warning and exit 0, so a rename could remove a public export with `publint`, `attw`, `deps.onlyImport` and typecheck all green. A module listed beside a hand-written barrel that re-exports it — `agent-console-server`'s `contracts` — is no collision, because both paths reach the same binding.

Generation is **unguarded** — it runs on every build. It reads as a function of the source file list, and a skip keyed on that list would save milliseconds while trusting a key to see every way the output can move; the `package-builds` cache already restores `dist` and the barrels together on an exact content hash.

**Watch generates a barrel once, at start.** tsdown calls `build:prepare` inside its single build pass and only then hands the graph to rolldown's watcher, so no rebuild under `watch:packages` generates again — and the restart it does have is keyed on the entry glob changing, which a literal `entry` can never trigger. An edit to an existing file therefore flows through; a **new** file's export does not, and a sibling resolving the `source` arm reads a barrel that never learned about it. Restarting the watch regenerates it. An edit inside an existing module — a new export included — needs nothing, since `export *` re-exports whatever the file holds.

## A subpath entry is a hand-written barrel

The generated barrel is the package's `.` entry and reaches every module. A second entry that must reach only part of the package — `agent-console-server`'s `contracts`, the wire a browser imports without the node half — is a hand-written file of `export * from` lines at `src/<entry>.ts`, named for the `dist/<entry>.js` the entry builds to. The generated barrel lists it too, harmlessly, for the reason above.

## Why the packages are not built more concurrently

The wall time is one topological chain, because a sibling's `source` arm points at its generated — and gitignored — barrel, so a worker count past what the graph allows changes nothing. What already answers the dev loop is `watch:packages`, and CI's is the `package-builds` content cache.
